messages.subject: stat_smooth() custom "familiy"
parts:
Dear all:
After using a custom 'family' "logexp"  to fit logistic exposure regression of Nest daily survive. I wound like to plot with stat_smooth() with formula to use in smoothing function and confidence interval to use (0.95 by default). However the stat_smooth() can't run with the logexp link.

Sample code:the R version is 2.15.3

# Logistical Exposure Link Function
# See Shaffer, T.  2004. A unifying approach to analyzing nest success.
# Auk 121(2): 526-540.
library(MASS)
logexp <- function(days = 1)
{
  linkfun <- function(mu) qlogis(mu^(1/days))
  linkinv <- function(eta) plogis(eta)^days
  mu.eta <- function(eta) days * plogis(eta)^(days-1) *
    .Call("logit_mu_eta", eta, PACKAGE = "stats")
  valideta <- function(eta) TRUE
  link <- paste("logexp(", days, ")", sep="")
  structure(list(linkfun = linkfun, linkinv = linkinv,
                 mu.eta = mu.eta, valideta = valideta, name = link),
            class = "link-glm")
}
#Example using chat data from Shaffer(2004).
nestdata<-read.table("http://data.prbo.org/tools/NestSurvival/chat.txt")
head(nestdata)
chat.glm.logexp<-glm(survive~parastat+nest_ht,family=binomial(logexp(days=nestdata$expos)),data=nestdata)
summary(chat.glm.logexp)
p<- ggplot(nestdata, aes(x=nest_ht, y=survive))+geom_point() +xlab("Nest Height")+ylab("Nest daily survive")+
  guides(fill=FALSE)+theme_bw()
p+stat_smooth(method="glm", family="binomial") #this runs well

p+stat_smooth(method="glm", family="logexp") (Error in method(formula, data = data, weights = weight, ...) : 'family' not recognized)

Any suggestions? How can I use the logexp link here? Much appreciated,
Qingshan
